bibliography.abstract: Origin-destination (OD) flow forecasting supports urban mobility decisions by predicting the volume and patterns of human movement across a city. Most existing public OD benchmarks provide only a partial view of citywide mobility, covering a single transport service or at most two modes. With partial mode coverage, observed demand changes are difficult to separate into shifts across transport modes and changes in total travel. We introduce SeoulMMOD, a large-scale public benchmark for citywide multimodal mobility in Seoul. SeoulMMOD provides three years of hourly OD flows estimating total mobility for 6 urban travel modes across 25 districts and 426 sub-districts, together with travel-time, travel-distance, calendar, rainfall, and point-of-interest (POI) signals. Using SeoulMMOD, we benchmark 14 forecasting baselines under a common protocol and analyse the effects of spatial scaling, joint versus mode-separate training, and cross-year generalization. Results show that several spatio-temporal models that work at district level do not scale to sub-district OD forecasting, and that naive joint multi-mode training does not consistently improve accuracy. Together, the dataset and benchmark establish a reproducible testbed for multi-mode, multi-year OD forecasting at the city scale.
bibliography.title: SeoulMMOD: A Large-Scale Multimodal Origin-Destination Flow Benchmark

orgs.label: Pohang University of Science and Technology

en.what: This study introduces SeoulMMOD, an open benchmark dataset containing three years of hourly origin-destination flows in Seoul spanning six transit modes across 25 districts and 426 sub-districts. The authors evaluated 14 spatio-temporal forecasting baselines alongside contextual covariates including POI data, travel metrics, calendar attributes, and rainfall records. The benchmark revealed that several district-level models fail to scale to finer sub-district resolutions and that naive joint multi-mode training yields inconsistent accuracy improvements.
en.why: Researchers can now evaluate forecasting models on complete citywide travel patterns across multiple modes simultaneously, preventing mode-shift distortions that occur when analyzing isolated transit datasets.
